name: hook_iat
description: Cross-process IAT (Import Address Table) hook against TestTarget. The attacker walks TestTarget's PE import descriptor table cross-process, locates the IAT slot for kernel32.dll!SleepEx (which TestTarget's main loop calls every 10 ms), allocates a small RWX trampoline in the target, writes a counter-increment + jump-to-original shellcode, flips the IAT page RO->RW, overwrites the 8-byte (x64) / 4-byte (x86) pointer slot with the trampoline shellcode address, and restores the IAT page's protection. Distinct from hook_inline: the overwritten write hits the target's IAT (typically inside .rdata or .idata, always in a page originally PAGE_READONLY), NOT the target's .text prologue — the write region is the primary distinguishing signal at classification time (see analysis/pe_utils.py). IAT hook is one of the two most common hook variants documented in game-cheat literature (alongside inline hook of graphics API entry points) — used to intercept imports like SleepEx, GetAsyncKeyState, or graphics presentation calls without touching module code sections.

extra.notes: Expected fingerprint: many small READVM_REMOTE events (PE header walk + import descriptor walk + name-string reads + IAT slot probe — typically 6-12 reads), 1x ALLOCVM_REMOTE (RWX trampoline, ~4KB), 1x WRITEVM_REMOTE (trampoline shellcode write, ~4KB), 1x PROTECTVM_REMOTE (IAT page RO->RW), 1x WRITEVM_REMOTE (pointer-sized slot overwrite: 8 bytes x64 / 4 bytes x86), 1x PROTECTVM_REMOTE (IAT page restore). No THREAD_CREATE_REMOTE. Distinguishing signal vs hook_inline: the small WRITEVM target address falls inside the target's IAT (parsed offline by analysis/pe_utils.py from DataDirectory[IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_IAT]), whereas an inline hook's small WRITEVM lands in a module's .text section.
